main.t: A single, triangular bone that forms the lower and back part of the nasal septum (vomer).

simpler.t: The vomer is a bone in the middle of your nose, at the lower back.

deeper.t: Seen from behind, it forms the whole height of the nasal septum.

facts.t: It lies in the midline, in the lower and back part of the nasal septum.
Above it is the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid; in front is the septal cartilage.
It is one of only two unpaired facial bones; the other is the mandible.

simpler.t: It is in the middle of your nose, at the back and bottom.

deeper.t: Looking into the front of the nose, you see only a small part of it.

items.name: Triangular shape
items.t: A flat, triangular plate in the midline.

items.name: Upper edge
items.t: Lies below the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid.

items.name: Front edge
items.t: The septal cartilage fills the gap between it and the perpendicular plate.

items.name: Back edge
items.t: Divides the two back openings of the nasal cavity.

simpler.t: It is a flat triangle of bone standing upright in the middle of the nose.

deeper.t: In the dry skull, the septal cartilage is missing, leaving a gap in front of it.

facts.t: With the ethmoid and the septal cartilage, it divides the nasal cavity into right and left halves.
The septal cartilage at its front edge extends into the nose and separates the nostrils.

simpler.t: It helps split your nose into two separate airways.

items.name: Ethmoid bone
items.t: Its perpendicular plate forms the upper part of the septum.

items.name: Septal cartilage
items.t: Forms the front of the septum, between the vomer and the perpendicular plate.

items.name: Nasal cavity
items.t: The septum divides it into two halves.

items.name: Sphenoid bone
items.t: Its upper border meets the body of the sphenoid.

simpler.t: It forms the nasal septum with part of the ethmoid and a plate of cartilage.

facts.t: Like the other flat bones of the face, it forms directly from membrane (intramembranous ossification).
facts.check: OpenStax 6.4 says the flat bones of the face form from membrane, but 7.5 says the facial bones form from cartilage; which applies to the vomer needs an approved source.

facts.t: It forms from two thin plates, which are almost completely united by puberty.
facts.check: Not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–9, 12–16, 20). Gray’s 1918 (7.2) says so (supporting only).

facts.t: The nasal septum is often bent to one side (a deviated septum).

items.injury: A septum bent to one side, from development or an injury.
items.damaged: The bony and cartilage parts of the septum, including the vomer.
items.cannotDo: Breathe freely through the narrower side.
items.why: The septum divides the nasal cavity, so bending it narrows one side.
items.check: A deviated septum is not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–9, 12–16, 20); the septum’s role is.

items.injury: A blow to the nose that breaks the septum.
items.damaged: The septal cartilage and the vomer.
items.cannotDo: Breathe evenly through both sides of the nose.
items.why: The broken septum shifts into one side of the nasal cavity.

items.q: Explain why the vomer looks so different from the front and from behind.
model: From the front, the perpendicular plate forms the upper septum.
Only a small part of the vomer shows below it.
From behind, looking into the back openings of the nose, the vomer is seen in full.
There it forms the whole height of the septum.

items.q: Compare the three parts of the nasal septum.
model: Perpendicular plate of the ethmoid: the upper part.
Vomer: the lower and back parts.
Septal cartilage: the front, between the two bones.
The cartilage also separates the nostrils, and is absent in the dry skull.

items.q: Predict what the nasal septum of a dry skull looks like from the front, and explain why.
model: The perpendicular plate is seen as the upper septum.
A small part of the vomer shows below.
There is a gap at the front between them.
The septal cartilage that fills it in life is not found in the dry skull.

check.stem: Which part of the nasal septum does the vomer form?
check.why: It forms the posterior-inferior part of the nasal septum.

check.stem: What fills the gap between the vomer and the perpendicular plate at the front?
check.why: The septal cartilage fills the gap.

check.stem: Which are the two unpaired facial bones?
check.why: The unpaired facial bones are the vomer and the mandible.
